text: Fodor contrasts encapsulated input modules with the central systems responsible for belief fixation and reasoning. Which feature of central systems does he claim makes them resistant to scientific study?
choices: They are domain-specific and process only one kind of input
They operate mandatorily and cannot be switched off
They deliver only shallow, stereotyped outputs
They are isotropic and holistic -- in principle any belief can be relevant to the evaluation of any other
explanation: Fodor calls central cognition isotropic (Quinean/holistic): unlike an encapsulated module, belief fixation can draw on anything you know, which makes it computationally unbounded and, he argues, scientifically intractable. Options 0, 1, and 2 (domain specificity, mandatory operation, shallow outputs) are all properties of modular INPUT systems -- exactly what central systems lack.
